records.researcher_notes: The Illinois EPA issued a final construction permit on October 4, 2021 to Aligned Data Centers (ORD) PropCo for a Northlake data center. The statement of basis lists 49 diesel emergency generators of 3,000 kW and 2 of 500 kW. That adds up to 147 MW plus 1 MW, or 148 MW. A listing on Baxtel gives the address as 505 Northwest Ave, Northlake. The point is the Census geocoder match for that address, so the location is marked approximate. A Data Center Frontier article of April 28, 2021 says Aligned broke ground in Northlake that day. That was also the first public word of the project, so it was announced and under construction in the same month. The Illinois EPA received the air permit application on May 10, 2021, after the groundbreaking, so I did not add a separate pre-construction milestone. A Data Center Dynamics article of April 20, 2022 says the first phase of ORD-01 was complete. The Baxtel listing also calls it operational and built in 2022. So the status is operating and the start year is 2022. The permit does not say how many of the generators are installed. The same 2022 article says Aligned started a second building, ORD-02, next door. It is on the watch list until its generators are found. The owner is Aligned Data Centers (ORD) PropCo, the company named on the final Illinois EPA permit of October 4, 2021. It is not yet in the GEM entity list. Its parent company, Aligned Data Centers, is in the list with ID 100002029095.

records.researcher_notes: The Illinois EPA issued a construction permit on May 13, 2026 to Monarch Rock Air Gen LLC for a plant it calls the Milkweed Energy Center: twenty Wartsila natural gas engine generator sets of 12.37 MW each, 247.4 MW in all, with selective catalytic reduction and an oxidation catalyst. The application was received on February 5, 2026. The permit is in the Illinois EPA document library under site number 201030DIR, in two copies. The engines are non-emergency units and the permit caps their combined running time at 130,680 hours a year, which is about 6,500 hours per engine, so this is a primary power plant and not a backup fleet. The permit's location line gives the coordinates 42.1526, -89.1186 in Rockford, Winnebago County, so the point is entered as exact from the permit. The permit does not name the data center. The link is the company: a Rock River Current article of June 2026, based on state incentive records, says Monarch Rock Air plans a multibuilding data center campus with associated power generation along Friday Road near the county line, and the permit coordinates fall about 1.4 kilometers west of 8685 Friday Road, inside that area. A Rockford News First article of March 5, 2026 says the company, Monarch Energy of Santa Cruz, California, controls a 1,300 acre site near Edson and Friday Roads with 1,200 MW of ComEd grid power due from January 2028, and the permittee's address on the permit is 101 Cooper Street, Santa Cruz. A Rockford News First article of July 1, 2026 says the state incentive agreement requires the facility to be in service by March 11, 2031. The owner is the permittee, Monarch Rock Air Gen LLC. The parent is Monarch Energy because the Rock River Current article ties the project company to it and the permittee shares its Santa Cruz address; no filing states the share, so the parent is less certain than the owner. The Parent field is filled by the database from the entity record, so it is not entered here. Neither company is in the GEM entity list, so two new entities are needed. Not found: a start year, a construction start, a grid connection for the engines, or any news report of the permit. Status is pre-construction because the air permit is issued and no source reports construction. This record closes the Monarch watch item in this batch, which had found no permit when the notice feed alone was searched.

The permit covers one 1,000 kW life safety diesel generator set and twenty-two critical diesel generator sets described as a mix of 3,213 kW Cummins and 3,000 kW Caterpillar sets, without saying how many of each. If all twenty-two are the larger set the fleet is 71.7 MW; if all are the smaller set it is 67.0 MW. The high end is recorded, as the manual asks for ranges. units.researcher_notes: Equinix is planning a data center campus at the corner of Holt Road and Ridge Road in Minooka. The Illinois EPA construction permit, application received November 7, 2025 and issued July 9, 2026, gives the address as 1300 N Ridge Road in Kendall County. It covers ninety-two 3.5 MW diesel emergency engine generators, 322 MW, and three 1 MW generators, 3 MW, plus two 200 kW and one 250 kW engines that are exempt from permitting. The permitted fleet is 325 MW, far above the 50 MW threshold. A WSPY News report from late September 2025 says village trustees approved the campus after a public hearing that month: four AI data centers of about 200,000 square feet each plus retail buildings. The status is pre-construction: the air permit is issued and the village has approved the plan, but no construction start has been reported. The point is the geocoded address of Ridge Road, so the location is approximate. News reports place Minooka in Grundy County, but the permit says Kendall County, and the permit is used here; a reviewer should check which county the parcel is in. The owner is Equinix, the permittee. Not found: a construction start or a planned opening year.

milestones.note: WSPY News reported the village approval after a public hearing in September 2025. The Illinois EPA received the air permit application on November 7, 2025 and issued the permit on July 9, 2026
